description: Pollo en Mole is a culinary masterpiece, a rich and complex Mexican sauce traditionally served with tender chicken. This iconic dish features a harmonious blend of chiles, spices, nuts, seeds, and a hint of chocolate, creating a deep, savory, and slightly sweet flavor profile. It is a true celebration of Mexican heritage, perfect for special occasions or a comforting family meal.

instructions.title: Prepare and Rehydrate Chiles
instructions.text: Lightly toast the dried Ancho, Mulato, and Pasilla chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1-2 minutes per side until fragrant. Be careful not to burn them. Transfer the toasted chiles to a bowl, cover with hot water, and let them rehydrate for 20-30 minutes until soft. Drain the chiles, reserving some of the soaking liquid.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics and Spices
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 1 tablespoon of lard or oil over medium heat. Add the halved Roma tomatoes, chopped onion, and peeled garlic cloves. Sauté until softened and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes. Add the almonds, pecans, 2 tablespoons of sesame seeds, raisins, and torn corn tortilla. Cook for another 3-5 minutes, stirring frequently, until the nuts are lightly toasted. Stir in the ground cumin, cinnamon, and cloves, cooking for 1 minute more until fragrant.

instructions.title: Blend the Mole Base
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the sautéed ingredients, along with the rehydrated chiles, to a blender. Add 2 cups of chicken broth. Blend until the mixture is very smooth. If needed, add a little more chicken broth or reserved chile soaking liquid to achieve a pourable consistency. For an extra smooth sauce, pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing down on the solids.

instructions.title: Cook the Mole Sauce
instructions.text: Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of lard or oil in the same pot or Dutch oven over medium-low heat. Carefully pour in the blended mole paste. Be cautious as it may splatter. Cook the mole, stirring constantly to prevent sticking, for at least 30-45 minutes. This slow cooking allows the flavors to deepen and the sauce to thicken significantly. If the mole becomes too thick, add more chicken broth, a little at a time, to reach your desired consistency.

instructions.title: Add Chicken and Season
instructions.text: While the mole is simmering, cook your chicken pieces. You can simmer them in chicken broth until tender, or pan-fry them until golden brown. Once the mole has cooked down and developed its rich flavor, stir in the chopped Mexican chocolate, 1/2 teaspoon of sugar, and salt to taste. Continue to cook, stirring, until the chocolate is fully melted and incorporated. Adjust seasoning as needed, balancing the savory, sweet, and spicy notes.

instructions.title: Simmer and Serve
instructions.text: Add the pre-cooked tender chicken pieces directly into the simmering mole sauce. Ensure the chicken is fully coated. Continue to simmer for another 10-15 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the mole. Serve the Pollo en Mole hot, garnished with a sprinkle of sesame seeds, alongside warm tortillas, Mexican rice, or refried beans.

tips: The secret to a great mole is the slow cooking and constant stirring of the sauce. This allows the flavors to truly meld and deepen, transforming the paste into a rich, complex sauce.
For an even smoother mole, after blending, pass the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve. This removes any remaining bits of chile skin or nut particles, giving you a velvety texture.
Mole is best made a day in advance. The flavors intensify and meld beautifully overnight, making it even more delicious when reheated. Store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
